questions.q: Where does every deployment, validation, and package execution against the SSIS Catalog get logged?
options: The SSISDB database
It isn't logged anywhere unless a custom log provider is added
A separate text log file per package, stored on the file system
The Windows Event Log exclusively
questions.explain: SSISDB is the single source of truth — every catalog operation's history writes there, which is exactly what makes the Active Operations dialog and standard reports possible.

questions.q: What does the Active Operations dialog show?
options: The list of deployed projects only, not executions
A historical archive of every execution ever run
Every currently-running operation on the server, with the ability to stop one
Only operations that failed in the last 24 hours
questions.explain: Active Operations is the real-time view — deployments, validations, and executions in progress right now — distinct from the historical standard reports.

questions.q: Which standard report lets you view executions across a custom date range, including the exact parameter values used per run?
options: Active Operations
All Executions
All Connections
Integration Services Dashboard
questions.explain: Unlike the Dashboard, which is locked to the last 24 hours, All Executions covers any date range you configure and shows the parameter values used for each specific run.

questions.q: What must be true for the Execution Performance report's per-component Active Time/Total Time detail to actually appear?
options: The report only works for packages deployed within the last 24 hours
The job step's Run as account must be a Windows administrator
The package must have run at least 10 times total
The logging level for that run must have been set to Performance or Verbose
questions.explain: That per-component detail is only captured when logging level was Performance or Verbose — at the default Basic level, it's simply never recorded, and no report can show data that was never logged.

questions.q: Which report shows connections that have failed across executions, along with the connection string and failure count?
options: All Validations
Active Operations
Integration Services Dashboard only
All Connections
questions.explain: All Connections is specifically scoped to connection failures across executions — the connection string, how many times it failed, and when it last failed.
